The main takeaway from our work is that

the proteolipids, like other proteins, can be recognized in situ by site-specific antibodies directed against synthetic peptides, and that the proteolypids are localized in the Golgi apparatus and in the myelin sheaths.

the proteolipids of the central nervous system are synthesized by oligodendroglial cells and transported in vesicles from the Golgi complex to the plasma membrane and then to the myelin membrane where the protein is inserted in the membrane.
site-directed antibodies to the proteolipids can provide useful information about the structure of myelin and myelin-forming cells.
